Natural_Language: This part prescribes minimum requirements for conducting market research before procuring supplies and services. See section 887 of Public Law 114-92 (41 U.S.C. 1703 note), 41 U.S.C. 3306(a)(1), 41 U.S.C. 3307, and 10 U.S.C. 3453.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_000_a: Part 10 prescribes minimum requirements for conducting market research; P_10_000_b: Market research is conducted before procuring supplies and services
Validation_Notes: Scope statement establishing dual requirement: Part 10 sets minimum standards AND those standards apply before procurement. Both elements are mandatory. Statutory references provide legal authority but do not create additional logical dependencies.

Natural_Language: Agencies must conduct market research appropriate to the circumstances before developing new requirements documents, soliciting offers for acquisitions with an estimated value over the simplified acquisition threshold, or awarding a task or delivery order over the simplified acquisition threshold.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001: Agencies conduct market research requirements as specified in subsections (a) through (f)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating all market research requirements. All six subsections must be satisfied for complete compliance with section 10.001.

Natural_Language: Agencies must describe their legitimate needs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_a: Agencies describe their legitimate needs
Validation_Notes: Simple mandatory requirement. Atomic proposition requires no logical operators. 'Must' establishes obligation without conditions.

Natural_Language: Agencies must conduct market research appropriate to the circumstances before developing new requirements documents, soliciting offers for acquisitions with an estimated value over the simplified acquisition threshold, or awarding a task or delivery order over the simplified acquisition threshold.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_b: Agencies conduct market research appropriate to circumstances before triggering events in (b)(1), (b)(2), or (b)(3)
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive trigger: any one of three events requires market research. Temporal 'before' establishes precedence requirement. Material implication creates conditional mandate: when any trigger occurs, market research must have been conducted. HIGH-RISK transformation due to material implication.

Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_b_1: Agency is developing new requirements documents
Validation_Notes: Trigger condition 1 for market research requirement. Standalone this is descriptive; becomes prescriptive through parent conditional in P_10_001_b.

Natural_Language: Soliciting offers for acquisitions with an estimated value over the simplified acquisition threshold.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_b_2: Agency is soliciting offers for acquisitions with estimated value over simplified acquisition threshold
Validation_Notes: Trigger condition 2 for market research requirement. Threshold creates binary classification (over/under SAT). Standalone descriptive, becomes prescriptive through parent.

Natural_Language: Awarding a task or delivery order over the simplified acquisition threshold.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_b_3: Agency is awarding task or delivery order over simplified acquisition threshold
Validation_Notes: Trigger condition 3 for market research requirement. Applies specifically to task/delivery orders (subset of all procurement actions). Standalone descriptive, becomes prescriptive through parent.

Natural_Language: Agencies should engage in responsible and constructive exchanges with industry. Agencies may use different strategies and methods to gather information, so long as they comply with existing law and regulation and do not provide an unfair competitive advantage to particular firms or violate the procurement integrity requirements (see 3.104).
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_c_1: Agencies engage in responsible and constructive exchanges with industry; P_10_001_c_2: Agencies use strategies and methods to gather information; P_10_001_c_3: Agencies comply with existing law and regulation; P_10_001_c_4: Agencies do not provide unfair competitive advantage to particular firms; P_10_001_c_5: Agencies do not violate procurement integrity requirements in section 3.104
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Mixed advisory and mandatory elements. 'Should' for industry engagement is advisory (P_10_001_c_1). 'May' grants discretion on methods (P_10_001_c_2) but 'so long as' creates mandatory constraints when methods are used. Conditional structure: IF agencies use strategies, THEN they must comply with law, avoid unfair advantage, and maintain procurement integrity. External dependency on Part 3 for integrity requirements. HIGH-RISK due to material implication and mixed modalities.

Natural_Language: When conducting market research, agencies must not ask potential sources to submit more than the minimum information necessary to make the determinations required in paragraph (f).
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_d_a: Agencies are conducting market research; P_10_001_d_b: Agencies ask potential sources to submit only minimum information necessary for determinations in paragraph (f)
Validation_Notes: Conditional prohibition with scope limitation. 'When conducting' creates trigger (P_10_001_d_a). 'Must not ask for more than minimum' translates to 'must ask for minimum or less' (P_10_001_d_b). Dependency on paragraph (f) for what determinations require. Prevents data overreach during market research. HIGH-RISK transformation due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Agencies must document the results of market research in a manner that suits the acquisition's size and complexity.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_e: Agencies document market research results in manner suited to acquisition size and complexity
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation requirement with flexibility on form. 'Must document' is absolute, but 'in a manner that suits' grants discretion on documentation approach based on context. No logical operators needed for this atomic requirement.

Natural_Language: Agencies must procure commercial products and commercial services to the maximum extent practicable. Using the results of market research, agencies will determine, in the following order of priority, whether a commercial product or commercial service on an existing governmentwide contract can meet the agency's requirements, the requirements could be modified so the agency could use an existing governmentwide contract, a commercial product or commercial service is available from another source, a commercial product or commercial service could be modified to meet the agency's requirements, or the requirement can only be satisfied by a nondevelopmental item.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_f: Agencies procure commercial products and services to maximum extent practicable by evaluating options (f)(1) through (f)(5) in order of priority
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition combining statutory preference (commercial products/services) with waterfall decision framework. Agencies must prefer commercial items AND must evaluate five options in priority order. Disjunction represents alternative pathways, but sequential evaluation is implied by 'order of priority' language. All five subsections contribute to overall determination.

Natural_Language: A commercial product or commercial service on an existing governmentwide contract can meet the agency's requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_f_1: Commercial product or service on existing governmentwide contract meets agency requirements
Validation_Notes: Priority 1 option in commercial preference waterfall. Evaluates whether existing contract vehicles can satisfy need without modification. This is descriptive of evaluation criterion, not independently prescriptive.

Natural_Language: The requirements could be modified so the agency could use an existing governmentwide contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_f_2: Requirements can be modified to enable use of existing governmentwide contract
Validation_Notes: Priority 2 option. If Priority 1 fails, evaluate whether requirement adjustment enables use of existing contracts. Implies flexibility in requirements definition.

Natural_Language: A commercial product or commercial service is available from another source.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_f_3: Commercial product or service is available from another source outside governmentwide contracts
Validation_Notes: Priority 3 option. Expands search beyond governmentwide contracts to broader commercial marketplace. 'Another source' distinguishes from (f)(1) contract-based sourcing.

Natural_Language: A commercial product or commercial service could be modified to meet the agency's requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_f_4: Commercial product or service can be modified to meet agency requirements
Validation_Notes: Priority 4 option. Evaluates commercial item customization as alternative to nondevelopmental procurement. Maintains commercial preference while accommodating unique requirements.

Natural_Language: The requirement can only be satisfied by a nondevelopmental item.
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_001_f_5: Requirement can only be satisfied by nondevelopmental item
Validation_Notes: Priority 5 (final) option. Nondevelopmental item is fallback when commercial options (priorities 1-4) are unavailable or unsuitable. 'Only' indicates exclusivity - other options have been exhausted.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must insert the clause at 52.210-1, Market Research, in solicitations and contracts for noncommercial acquisitions over $6 million. This policy was established in 10 U.S.C. 3453(c).
Atomic_Propositions: P_10_002_a: Acquisition is noncommercial and over $6 million; P_10_002_b: Contracting officer inserts clause 52.210-1 in solicitation and contract
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause insertion requirement. When acquisition meets criteria (noncommercial AND over $6M threshold), clause insertion is mandatory. External dependency on Part 52 for clause content. Statutory authority cited but does not create additional logical dependency. HIGH-RISK transformation due to material implication.
